description: Found 2026-07-31 by a sentinel sweep that constructed every registered adapter and drove the real export entry points. The keys api_key / onehouse_api_key (quanton's ONLY credential - benchbox/platforms/onehouse/quanton_adapter.py:616, sent as a Bearer header by onehouse_client.py:191) and storage_account_key (a full-access Azure storage account key - azure_synapse.py:125, interpolated into AccountKey=... connection strings at :740) are exported VERBATIM by BOTH sanitize_platform_options (internal result metadata via runtime_metadata.py:105) AND anonymize_result_payload (the public/anonymized export, exporter.py:320, default anonymize=True): neither secret-key list contains a matching part - 'apikey' and 'accountkey' match nothing in platform_options._SECRET_KEY_PARTS or anonymization_specs.yaml secret_key_parts. Driven proof: sanitize_platform_options({'api_key':'X','storage_account_key':'Y'}) returns both verbatim; anonymize_result_payload on the same payload returns both verbatim. Unlike the keyid gap (which the capture-time sanitize masks on the standard path), THESE keys leak on the public path with no upstream mask - this is the live end-to-end variant of the defect family. Depends on anonymization-path-misses-key-id-secrets so the one-source-of-truth list lands first and this becomes a narrow addition to a single list.

preserves.behavior: Existing redaction/pseudonymization behavior for already-covered keys
Non-credential lookalikes (sort_key, partition_key, primary_key, user_agent) keep exporting real values
